title: arrival-smoother-and-kv-compaction-standup-oct05-2029
notes:
Weekly standup — focus: arrival smoothing heuristic prototype, KV compaction background job, and small-batch latency tradeoffs. Attendees: Jamie (notes), Aisha, Tomás, Lena, Ravi, and a short async update from Priya.

1) Quick context and goal
- Problem: spiky traffic with many very-small prompts (<= 8 tokens) causes a high proportion of single-request micro-batches; this increases p95 token latency and reduces usable kernel utilization.
- Goal this sprint: validate a lightweight arrival-smoother that delays scheduling by up to 6ms for very small requests to increase coalescing without regressing p50 for interactive flows. Also roll out a safe KV compaction prototype that reclaims orphaned prefix entries during low-util windows.

2) Arrival-smoother prototype status
- Implementation: A small scheduler shim (scheduler/arrival_smoother.cc) adds an exponential backoff window tuned per-endpoint. For requests with prompt_len <= 8 and user_tier != dedicated, we annex a 0-6ms randomized delay before offering to the kernel. We also shadow the old path concurrently.
- Metrics collected (canary region): sample window 2029-10-03 -> 2029-10-04, endpoint: chat-small-v1, 120k requests
  - baseline avg batch size: 1.12 -> prototype avg batch size: 1.67 (+49%)
  - cache hit rate (KV lookup): baseline 28.4% -> prototype 31.1% (+2.7pp)
  - p50 token latency: baseline 12.3ms -> prototype 13.1ms (+0.8ms)
  - p95 token latency: baseline 58.9ms -> prototype 46.2ms (-12.7ms)
  - overall CPU utilization on serving nodes: baseline 63% -> prototype 71% (more sustained kernel time)
- Interpretation: p50 regressions are small and within SLA buffers for this endpoint; p95 improves significantly. CPU increase expected; need to confirm cost trade-offs.
- Issues observed: occasional tail blips at 99.9 where the randomized delay coincided with upstream retry loops — need to ensure idempotency headers are passed through to avoid duplicate processing.

3) KV compaction background job
- Motivation: long-lived prefix keys from aborted sessions and rare large-prefix churn cause KV store bloat and poor LRU behavior. We want a low-risk compaction that operates in off-peak windows and emits traces for any key removals.
- Prototype: compaction worker runs once per hour on off-peak region nodes (window configurable). It marks candidate prefixes with a tombstone key TTL metadata and then performs a two-step removal after a 24-hour probation. It writes an audit entry per-compacted-prefix to S3 (for compliance).
- Canary run (2029-10-04 02:00-04:00 UTC): reclaimed ~3.8M prefix bytes across 12k prefix keys; observed immediate KV eviction pressure drop of ~6% and a small improvement in cache hit tail.
- Safety checks added: dry-run mode, max deletions per-minute, and automatic pause if eviction rate spikes > 15% vs baseline.
- Follow-up: need KMS permission review for S3 audit writes (security) and an ops runbook entry for manual pause/rollback.

4) Kernel small-batch tuning summary
- Kernel changes to support the arrival-smoother require an adjustment in our microbatch coalesce window (kernel/queue_manager.c). We added a cheap heuristic to prefer coalescing older requests when the expected batch size still < target. This reduces jitter in scheduling and results in smoother GPU kernel launches.
- Bench highlights: under synthetic small-prompt workload, throughput per-GPU improved 28% with arrival-smoother + kernel heuristic combined vs baseline. Latency distribution tighter.

5) Observability and tracing
- We added new span tags: arrival_smoother.delay_ms, compaction.tombstone_count, compaction.deleted_count. Grafana dashboard panels created for these (dashboard id: SRV-ARR-SMOOTH-4).
- Action: SLO alert refinement needed — p50 at endpoint-level can tolerate +1.5ms, but p99 remains our hard stop. Create alert JIRA JIRA-3150 to add a composite alert that includes arrival_smoother.enable_rate and p99 token latency.

6) Decision log
- Roll forward arrival-smoother to a 10% traffic canary for all hosted endpoints of tier 'free' and 'standard' (not dedicated) starting 2029-10-08. Canary to run for 72h with automatic rollback if p99 token latency increases > 10% or error rate increases > 0.5pp. (Decision: agreed, owner: Aisha)
- Enable KV compaction as a weekly job in off-peak windows in canary region; keep dry-run flag for one week. (Decision: agreed, owner: Tomás)

7) Blockers and risks
- Security: need KMS/S3 audit write approval (Ravi, on it).
- Observability: missing long-range 99.9 traces for the new path — tracing sampling adjusted but we need an extra 2x sample rate for requests that pass through arrival-smoother. (Owner: Lena)
- Cost: increased CPU utilization may raise infra costs; finance wants a quick projection before wider rollout. Need ballpark hourly cost delta. (Owner: Jamie)

8) Action items (explicit)
- Aisha: configure canary rollout pipeline and schedule 10% traffic start 2029-10-08; create automatic rollback job. (due 2029-10-07)
- Tomás: flip compaction job from dry-run to live in canary region but with max_deletions=200/min guard. Add SLO telemetry for deleted_count. (due 2029-10-09)
- Lena: increase trace sampling for arrival-smoother path and validate 99.9 tail traces are captured for at least 500 samples/day. (due 2029-10-07)
- Ravi: chase KMS/S3 permissions and confirm audit writes are acceptable for compliance; escalate if >48h. (due 2029-10-07)
- Jamie: produce a 48h cost-impact estimate for CPU delta and expected token cost amortization; sync with finance. (due 2029-10-09)
- Priya: run a short PR benchmark for retry-loop interactions and validate idempotency header passthrough; report on duplicate processing risk. (due 2029-10-06)

9) Open questions & experiments
- Experiment: try a deterministic tiny-delay (fixed 3ms) vs randomized 0-6ms to see p50 tradeoffs. Priya to A/B test.
- Should we allow dedicated customers to opt-in? Likely yes as a tenant-level setting, but they may not want added jitter. Need product input.
- Long-term: consider a predictive arrival-smoother that uses per-user session patterns (ML) instead of randomized delays. Keep as research spike only.

10) Links & references
- Design sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/arrival-smoother-design-draft
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1824
- Canary metrics dashboard: SRV-ARR-SMOOTH-4

End of notes. Next sync: quick check-in 2029-10-09 (post-canary-start). Please drop incremental updates to #serving-runtime-prod channel and tag Aisha for rollout status.
